children: The U.S. Coast Guard said on September 2 that it intercepted a cargo ship in the Caribbean in early September that U.S. authorities said was illegally transporting fuel to Cuba. According to Sina Finance, the Coast Guard boarded the vessel for inspection and later escorted it to the port of Progreso, north of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula.

The Mexican Navy confirmed that the ship's ballast tanks contained a large amount of fuel. It also said the vessel was carrying several containers believed to hold what U.S. authorities described as illegal fuel.

The Coast Guard also said it boarded and seized another cargo ship earlier this summer that was believed to be transporting illegal fuel to Cuba. Cuban Foreign Minister Rodriguez said on September 7 that the U.S. trade embargo on Cuba had caused record economic losses and worsened the decline in real income for poor families while raising living costs.

title: U.S. Coast Guard Says It Intercepted Cargo Ship Carrying Fuel to Cuba
